core.title: Make every typed plan reference resolve to a declared artifact
core.given: The plan's artifacts contain typed references to plan artifacts, changed or not (the reference kinds in scope are the plan-reference shapes the profile lists).
core.when: The plan is validated or inspected as a whole, or the planner authors, edits, removes or renames plan artifacts.
core.then: Every such typed reference must name an artifact the plan declares.
prefer: Declare the referenced artifact in the plan when the relationship is real.
Correct the reference to the actual declared id when it is a typo or stale after a rename.
When removing or renaming an artifact, update every typed reference that points to it in the same change.
avoid: Leaving references to nothing — a relationship the plan claims but cannot show.
Creating empty placeholder artifacts only to make a reference resolve without the relationship being real.
Treating references of a kind whose resolution another rule owns as if this rule owned them.
unless: The reference lives in a vendored or generated tree; those are never scanned.
core.why: A reference to nothing is a relationship the plan claims and cannot show; unresolved references break plan traceability.
evidence: The whole-plan integrity check reports no unresolved typed references for the plan.
A reviewer can map each typed reference to an artifact the plan declares.
verification: A whole-plan check resolves every in-scope typed reference — including pre-existing, unchanged ones — against the artifacts the plan declares; it does not check only references touched by the current change.
Only the reference kinds in scope for this rule are checked; reference kinds whose resolution is owned by another rule are excluded.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact classification of excluded trees is owned by the stack's checker and is the stack-wide excluded list in the profile.
Per-rule severity 3 with strict disposition: the rule fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: A planner writes a plan artifact that references an artifact id that no plan artifact declares.
A plan artifact or acceptance artifact references an id that was renamed or removed elsewhere in the plan.
Whole-plan validation finds a pre-existing, unchanged typed reference that names no declared artifact, even though nothing in the current change touched it.
doesNotFire: A reference of a kind whose resolution another rule owns.
References inside vendored or generated trees — the trees the profile marks as never scanned.
Every typed reference in the plan names an artifact the plan declares.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan artifact kinds that declare ids in the plan and that typed references point at; the core's 'artifact the plan declares' ranges over these, and they identify plan artifact files by path/file kind.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral; all stack specificity sits in (a) the six reference prefixes, carried by the profile's urn.* shapes (flow router proposed, since the closed vocabulary lacks it), (b) the excluded `contract:` kind, kept only as 'kinds whose resolution another rule owns' with the concrete kind in bunOnly, (c) the never-scanned trees via roots.excluded, with the core deferring exact classification to the stack's checker, and (d) validator and finding ids, which are realization details. Per-rule severity 3 and strict disposition are both retained in core verification as rule-level facts, per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys. The core's phrase 'an artifact the plan declares' presumes the profile's URN declaration conventions; bun.json does not state that syntax, so no profile value was required for it.
